questions.question: How many serial killers were listed in the Radford database in 2016?
questions.insight: In 2016, the Radford/FGCU database listed 4,743 serial killers and 13,105 victims.

questions.question: In which decade did the United States see the highest number of new serial killers begin killing?
questions.insight: The 1970s are the peak decade here: 605 new killers began, often linked to mobility and weaker data-sharing.

questions.question: What percentage of U.S. serial killers are men?
questions.insight: About 90.8% are men; women represent roughly 9%.

questions.question: Which ethnicity currently represents the largest share of U.S. serial killers?
questions.insight: In this dataset, white offenders are ~52% and black offenders ~38%.

questions.question: What is the most common motive among serial killers?
questions.insight: Pleasure (lust/thrill/power) is the most reported motive at about 36%.

questions.question: What is the average IQ of a serial killer?
questions.insight: Average IQ is about 94.5—near normal, not the 'genius mastermind' stereotype.

questions.question: Which method of killing is most common among serial killers?
questions.insight: Firearms are most common (~43%), with strangulation next (~22%).

questions.question: Which U.S. state has recorded the most serial-killer victims?
questions.insight: California has the most recorded victims (1,628), followed by Texas and Florida.

questions.question: How old are most serial-killer victims?
questions.insight: Most victims are young adults; average age is ~33.8 (median ~29).

questions.question: Which gender represents most serial-killer victims?
questions.insight: Women are about 70% of victims in the Radford/FGCU database.

questions.question: Which decade saw the highest number of active serial killers in the U.S. in a given year?
questions.insight: The 1980s averaged ~145 active serial killers per year; later decades drop with better forensics and databases.

questions.question: What percentage of U.S. serial killers served in the military?
questions.insight: About 18% of male serial killers served in the military.

conclusions.message: Early stage—these stats challenge common myths. Keep exploring.

conclusions.title: Informed Student
conclusions.message: Good baseline—you’re seeing how data differs from media narratives.

conclusions.title: Sharp Observer
